To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
endothelial Hif-2 mediates renoprotection from hypoxic kidney injury.
endothelial Hif-2 mediates renoprotection in models of ischemic kidney injury.
endothelial Hif2α is required for protection from ischemic renal damage and fibrosis, and that pharmacologic activation of Hif2α protects from ischemic kidney damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endothelial hypoxia-induicible factor 2 (HIF-2) in the pathogenesis of acute kidney injury (AKI).
the mechanisms of renal injury and fibrosis in the postischaemic kidney.
the role of endothelial Hif-2 in the kidney and its role in renal fibrosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endothelial cell HIF-2 is a critical regulator of hypoxia-mediated protection and recovery from acute kidney injury.
endothelial Hif-2 is protective and that HIF activation protects from ischemic kidney disease.
endothelial Hif2α mediates protection and repair from ischemic kidney damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF-2 is a key regulator of the vascular endothelium that protects from ischemic kidney disease.
endothelial Hif-2 mediates renoprotection in response to ischemia and ureteral obstruction, and that this renoprotective effect is mediated by the inhibition of inflammation.
HIF-2, but not HIF-1, in the endothelium is protective in models of acute kidney injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HIF-2 is an important mediator of protection against ischemic kidney injury, and that targeting HIF-2 might be beneficial in patients at risk for acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease.
endothelial Hif-2α is protective in the post-ischemic kidney and represents a novel target for the prevention of renal fibrosis.
endothelial Hif-2 mediates the protective effects of hypoxia-inducing agents in the kidney and represents a potential target for renoprotective therapy.
